question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (AMD)

calls.reasoning: Q2'26 GAAP EPS $1.38 included a $0.29 investment gain; underlying non-GAAP-to-GAAP gap ~$0.55-0.57 (SBC $0.30 + amortization $0.33 - tax $0.10). - OpenAI warrant (Oct 2025): up to 160M shares at $0.01, vesting on MI450 purchases (first tranche at 1 GW, deployment from H2'26); AMD books warrant value as contra-revenue when the revenue is recognized. Whether non-GAAP excludes it: not found. Meta warrants also reported. Oracle MI450 deployment from Q3'26.
- AMD stock fell ~11% heading into earnings (TradingKey preview); relevant if AMD holds marked-to-market equity stakes in AI names.
- Resolves off the GAAP diluted EPS in the Q3'26 earnings release (8-K, expected Nov 3 2026 after close), not non-GAAP.
- Event window: Q3 FY2026 release after Sep 30 2026; as of Nov 2 2026 the release is ~1 day away and not yet published.

calls.reasoning: Non-GAAP consensus ~$1.94-1.97 and AMD's beat history imply ~$2.00 non-GAAP. Recurring GAAP adjustments (SBC ~$0.30 + intangibles amortization ~$0.33, minus tax ~$0.08-0.10) give ~$1.45 core GAAP, consistent with the cited GAAP consensus of $1.42. Investment marks on IPO'd stakes are the main swing; Q3 equity markets and AMD's own stock were strong, so I tilt slightly up. The lower escape (3%) covers a GAAP-only warrant charge or impairment as MI450 shipments begin. No GAAP EPS market exists; Polymarket's non-GAAP beat contract (0.76) is near-miss evidence only.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agreed on the core arithmetic (non-GAAP ~$2.00 less a ~$0.53-0.60 gap gives ~$1.45 GAAP, with a $1.42 GAAP consensus) and on medians of 1.45-1.48. Factual dispute 1: whether OpenAI/Meta warrant accounting hits Q3 GAAP. The dossiers say no tranche had vested as of Jun 27 and shipments start in H2'26; whether Q3 carries a charge, and whether non-GAAP excludes it, could not be settled without web access, so I priced it as a 3% lower escape plus a left tail. Factual dispute 2: GAAP consensus of $1.42 vs $1.67; $1.42 fits the gap arithmetic, while $1.67 looks like a non-GAAP figure mislabeled. Judgment: direction of investment marks. Strong Q3 markets (AMD at a record in early October) tilt it modestly positive, which puts my median slightly above the core $1.45. Carried forward Run 1's dispersion (0.5) as the honest width given the unknown investment and warrant items.
